gen-zen-dots-gf-mooli: Zen Dots gives every letter generous space around it, a techy but friendly display voice. Mooli brings open, round sans letters, so body text can sit a size or two down without losing clarity.
gen-zen-dots-gf-noto-sans-javanese: Zen Dots is techy and friendly, with space around every letter. Noto Sans Javanese, plain sans through and through, keeps counters linked to outside space, which is the quality both fonts share.
gen-zen-dots-gf-noto-sans-old-south-arab: Techy but friendly, Zen Dots gives each letter room above Noto Sans Old South Arabian, whose curved strokes end before turning inward. Nudge the body size up a little so those curves show.
gen-zen-dots-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Zen Dots gives every letter shape generous room around it. Where Zen Dots wins on display presence, Noto Sans Shavian, plain sans with loose, unknotted curves, wins on the lines below.
gen-zen-dots-gf-overpass: Overpass keeps its strokes consistent within a word, with e shapes that never clog. Overpass can sit smaller than Zen Dots, whose low, wide bowls never thin at the sides.
gen-zen-dots-gf-reddit-sans: Techy and friendly up top: Zen Dots leaves generous room around each and every letter. And Reddit Sans, with its wide-gapped e and uniform stroke, would carry paragraph after paragraph smoothly.
gen-zen-dots-gf-sn-pro: SN Pro uses open, curving apertures across the whole alphabet. Beneath Zen Dots, whose spacious, friendly techy letters announce each section, that sans keeps the text modern and easy going.
gen-zen-dots-gf-special-gothic: Techy but friendly, Zen Dots is built for big, spacious display lines. But Special Gothic, plain sans with rounded, inviting letters, is the one that makes running text feel approachable.
gen-zen-dots-gf-tasa-orbiter: Friendly and techy, Zen Dots leaves generous room around every letter. It handles display moments, while TASA Orbiter, a sans-serif with unclogged small counters, does the quieter work of setting text.
gen-zen-dots-gf-telex: Zen Dots leaves generous room around every letter, giving headings a techy, friendly feel. And Telex, a sans with curvy, unclamped letters, loosens up the text beneath so the two sit comfortably together.
